title: Deliberate and indeliberate acts of love and desire
source_text: LVII. Praeterea notandum est actus amoris & desiderii, quibus afficitur voluntas, vel deliberatos & liberos esse, qui praevia consultatione, ex certo rationis judicio eliciuntur: vel indeliberatos, & ita non liberos, qui nimirum ad objecti alicujus propositionem, in voluntate subito oriuntur, priusquam mens consultare & deliberare possit.
pass_a_gloss: LVII. Further it is to be noted that the acts of love and desire, by which the will is affected, are either deliberate and free, which are elicited with prior consultation, from a certain judgment of reason: or indeliberate, and so not free, which namely at the proposal of some object, arise suddenly in the will, before the mind can consult and deliberate.
pass_b_english: Thesis LVII. Note also that the acts of love and desire that affect the will are of two kinds. Some are deliberate and free, drawn out after weighing the matter, from a definite judgment of reason. Others are indeliberate and therefore not free: they spring up in the will all at once when some object is put before it, before the mind is able to weigh and deliberate.

lemmas.gloss: or indeliberate, and so not free
before the mind can consult and deliberate

choices.why: An act arising before the mind deliberates (LVII), as opposed to a free, deliberate act.

bible_refs: Cornelius Jansenius, Augustinus (Louvain, 1640), tome 3, De gratia Christi Salvatoris, book 4.
